title: An amygdala-mediated simulation-to-decision cascade aligns interbrain dynamics to solve social dilemmas
title_zh: 杏仁核介导的模拟-决策级联使脑间动力学与社会困境对齐
abstract: Mutual cooperation (MC) requires independent decision-makers to coordinate under uncertainty about each other's intentions. Using simultaneous intracranial electroencephalography from epilepsy-patient dyads playing a real-time iterated prisoner's dilemma, we identified neurocognitive mechanisms that enable interacting brains to align during mutual cooperation. Amygdala interbrain representational alignment (IBRA), similarity in fine-grained neural spectral patterns across partners, emerged selectively during MC and predicted trial-by-trial outcomes. Early θ-suppression-characterized IBRA reflected rapid, history-sensitive alignment, whereas later IBRA, characterized by low-frequency suppression and γ increases, supported coordinated commitment and action. Furthermore, mutual cooperation relied on an amygdala-mediated, simulation-to-decision cascade, operationalized here as a model-based prospective estimate of partner cooperation that guided self-choice. Amygdala low-frequency suppression tracked this prospective estimate of partner cooperation and θ-γ coupling linked this partner estimate to self-decision processes. Conditional cooperators strategically relied on partner tracking, whereas unconditional cooperators leveraged dispositional tolerance of uncertainty to transition into anticipatory neural alignment. These findings reveal the neural interdependency underpinning MC, redefining cooperation not as isolated decision-making but as a dynamic, interbrain, cognitive alignment.
abstract_zh: 相互合作（MC）要求独立的决策者在对彼此意图的不确定性下协调。利用癫痫患者对的同时植入脑电图，在实时迭代囚徒困境游戏中，我们确定了使相互大脑在相互合作期间对齐的神经认知机制。杏仁核脑间表征对齐（IBRA）指合作伙伴之间细粒度神经频谱模式的相似性，专门在相互合作期间出现，并预测了试次结果。早期以θ抑制为特征的IBRA反映了快速、敏感于历史的对齐，而后期以低频抑制和γ增加为特征的IBRA则支持协调的承诺和行动。此外，相互合作依赖于杏仁核介导的模拟-决策级联，此处将其运算化为基于模型的合作伙伴合作的前瞻性估计，该估计指导了自我选择。杏仁核低频抑制追踪了此合作伙伴估计，θ-γ耦合将此合作伙伴估计与自我决策过程联系起来。条件合作者战略性地依赖合作伙伴追踪，而无条件合作者则利用对不确定性的倾向性耐受来转向预期的神经对齐。这些发现揭示了相互合作的神经依赖性，将合作重新定义为非孤立的决策，而是一种动态的、脑间的、认知对齐过程。
